title: Google Launches Gemini 3.7 Flash for Coding and AI Agent Workflows
excerpt: The budget-friendly model arrives three weeks after Gemini 3.6 Flash, but investors are still waiting for the flagship 3.5 Pro.
body:
• Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash on Thursday, a model optimized for software coding, debugging, and multi-step autonomous workflows
  • Introductory pricing is set at $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens — half the cost of Gemini 3.6 Flash — through the end of the year
  • The model is immediately available through Gemini Spark, Google's AI agent subscription service, in more than 160 countries
  • Google still has not announced a release date for the flagship Gemini 3.5 Pro, which investors view as a key test of DeepMind's competitiveness

Another Flash, Still No Pro

Alphabet's Google launched Gemini 3.7 Flash on Thursday, its latest AI model targeting software developers and businesses building autonomous AI systems, according to Reuters. The release marks the third Flash-tier model in a matter of months, but offered no details on when the company's highly anticipated flagship — Gemini 3.5 Pro — will ship.

https://x.com/Google/status/2087949499310223794

Google had said in July that Gemini 3.5 Pro was being tested with partners and would arrive "soon." Investors have been closely tracking the model as a measure of whether Google's DeepMind AI unit can keep pace with rivals Anthropic and OpenAI.

Gemini 3.7 Flash is released just three weeks after Gemini 3.6 Flash. The new model shows improved performance on coding tasks, including debugging, issue resolution, and production-ready code generation, according to a Google blog post cited by Reuters.

Aggressive Pricing Strategy

To drive adoption, Google is offering Gemini 3.7 Flash at an introductory rate of 75 cents per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens through the end of 2026 — half the original cost of Gemini 3.6 Flash, according to Reuters.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Geg9UEDzfbI

The pricing undercuts much of the market. For comparison, Gemini 3.6 Flash launched at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. Google's earlier Gemini 3 Flash was priced at $0.50 per million input tokens and $3 per million output tokens. The aggressive discounting reflects Google's strategy of trading margins for market share as the AI model race intensifies.

The model is pitched as a lower-cost option for businesses building autonomous AI agents that can plan tasks, use software tools, and complete multi-step workflows with less human intervention, according to Reuters.

DeepMind in Flux

The release comes during a period of upheaval at Google DeepMind. Last week, the company announced a sweeping leadership overhaul in which DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis stepped aside in favor of his deputy, Koray Kavukcuoglu, according to Reuters. At the same time, the two original technical co-leads of Gemini quit to co-found a startup.

Google co-founder Sergey Brin has in recent months urged key AI staff to go all-in on Gemini as Alphabet seeks to close the gap with rivals, Reuters exclusively reported on Wednesday.

"We have made significant progress in AI this year, and I am confident in the trajectory of our Gemini models."

— Sundar Pichai, Google CEO, during July earnings call

CEO Sundar Pichai mounted a robust defense of Google's AI strategy during the company's July earnings call, pushing back on concerns that the company had fallen behind rivals after delaying the flagship model and ceding ground in AI coding.

Gemini Spark and the Agent Push

Gemini 3.7 Flash is rolling out immediately to Gemini Spark, Google's subscription-based AI agent service available to Google AI Pro and Ultra customers in more than 160 countries, according to Reuters. The model's focus on agent workflows — systems that can plan, execute, and iterate on multi-step tasks with minimal human oversight — aligns with a broader industry shift toward AI agents as the next frontier beyond chatbots.

The rapid cadence of Flash model releases — Gemini 3 Flash in December, Gemini 3.5 Flash at I/O in May, Gemini 3.6 Flash in July, and now Gemini 3.7 Flash in August — signals Google is willing to iterate aggressively on its mid-tier models even as the premium Pro release remains delayed. For developers and businesses building on Google's AI stack, the pace offers faster capabilities at lower cost. For investors, the missing Pro model remains the elephant in the room.
